OPERATING THE FAULTMETER
This section gives step-by-step operating instructions. The Georgia faultmeter has 
several unique features, which have been added to simplify operations, increase range of  
measurement to 22 mm, and increase reach to 100 mm to allow for spanning spalls and 
excess joint material on the slab surface.
Use the right hand when testing the outside lane. This allows the operator to stand safely 
on the shoulder facing traffic

to allow for spanning spalls and 
excess joint material on the slab surface.
Use the right hand when testing the outside lane. This allows the operator to stand safely 
on the shoulder facing traffic while making the test. There is an arrow on the meter 
showing traffic direction. Set the meter on the leave side of  the joint. A probe contacts 
the slab on the approach side. The joint must be centered approximately between the two 
marks on each side of  the meter.

The State of Israel is investing significant efforts and resources in the development, upgrading, and maintenance of urban transportation infrastructure. As a result, there is a growing need to carry out numerous works, which require the regulation of traffic to ensure the safety of both workers and road users. 

The guide to traffic arrangements at work sites on urban roads outlined below details the various options for the placement of temporary traffic arrangements required for carrying out works on the road, with the aim of reducing risks, maintaining a high level of safety, and providing maximum service to all road users. 

In light of the above, by virtue of my authority as the national traffic supervisor (according to Regulation 16 of the Traffic Regulations, 1961), I hereby approve the traffic arrangements appearing in the diagrams (without change) for placement on the road in accordance with and subject to the instructions of the competent authorities as determined in the permit. 

I hereby instruct all local traffic authorities to allow the establishment of temporary traffic arrangements for carrying out works on the road using diagrams from this guide. 

This guide cancels all 'diagrams' in the urban area that were used prior to the publication of this guide, in order to achieve standardization of temporary traffic arrangements at work sites on the road in the State of Israel.

This guide cancels all 'diagrams' in the urban field that were used prior to the publication of this guide. The purpose is to unify the temporary traffic arrangements at work sites on the roads in the State of Israel. In any case where a diagram from this guide does not fully match the actual conditions on the ground (according to the professional standards detailed in the guide), diagrams from the guide should not be used, and the local authority must prepare a detailed traffic arrangement plan and approve it legally in accordance with the provisions of the law and regulations. This plan will be limited and valid only for the planning location. For clarification, a local traffic authority does not have the authority to approve generic traffic arrangements (diagrams). If a local traffic authority believes that a traffic arrangement (diagram) is needed that is not included in the guide, the authority must contact the national traffic supervisor along with its proposal to update the guide, which will be examined within a permanent steering committee that will operate to update and improve this guide from time to time.

1. Purpose and Content of the Guide  
This guide includes generic traffic arrangements (diagrams) approved by the National Traffic Inspector for establishing temporary traffic arrangements. For roads where the maximum permitted speed is 70 km/h, and in urban streets where the maximum permitted speed is up to 80 km/h, the guide for traffic arrangements at intercity work sites in its most current edition should be used. These diagrams are also applicable in areas with controlled access such as roads within nature reserves, public parks, etc. The guide is intended to provide tools for traffic authorities.

The diagrams are valid for all urban roads (as determined by public signage) with controlled access, such as roads within nature reserves, public parks, etc. The guide is intended to provide tools for local signage authorities to establish generic traffic arrangements (not tailored to a specific location), in order to facilitate and simplify the approval process for traffic arrangements necessary for road work and to save the need for detailed planning that requires updated measurement plans or aerial photographs. The use of the guide allows the local signage authority to approve the execution of work according to the diagrams (without the need for planning and consultation regarding the signs included in the diagram). To avoid doubt, traffic arrangements according to the diagrams may not be placed without permission from the competent authorities.
